You **cannot buy stock in Deloitte** because it is a privately held organization and not a publicly traded company.[[1]](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/how-to-invest-in-deloitte/)

#### Why You Can't Buy Deloitte

- **Partnership Structure:** Deloitte operates as a network of independent member firms structured as private partnerships or limited liability partnerships.[[1]](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/about/governance/network-brand-alliances.html)[[2]](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/how-to-invest-in-deloitte/)
- **Ownership Rules:** Equity in the firm is restricted to qualified partners rather than public shareholders.[[1]](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/how-to-invest-in-deloitte/)
- **Regulatory Constraints:** Independence rules (especially regarding auditing services) generally prevent massive accounting and professional services networks from floating on public stock exchanges.[[1]](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/how-to-invest-in-deloitte/)

#### Publicly Traded Alternatives

If you are looking to invest in the consulting or professional services space, several major competitors *are* publicly traded on the stock market:

- **Accenture** (`ACN` ) – A massive global giant in IT, digital, and management consulting.
- **Booz Allen Hamilton** (`BAH` ) – Known heavily for management and technology consulting (particularly with government and defense).
- **IBM** (`IBM` ) – Offers extensive enterprise consulting alongside its technology infrastructure.
- **Capgemini** (`CAP` ) – A multinational information technology and consulting corporation based in France.[[1]](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/stocks/how-to-invest-in-deloitte/)
